rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate pushes obfuscation strength up while protecting flops-5's hot FP loop: SUB, IBR, and ICALL get high SecurityGain/Diversity weights because they are cheap, correctness-safe transforms that defeat pattern-matching and static analysis of the arithmetic-heavy main; IGV adds constant/diversity obfuscation with low runtime sensitivity; FLA and BCF are enabled with strong security weights but deliberately high RuntimeCost (0.8/0.75) and SizeCost sensitivity so the feature-driven selector dampens them on the hot loop body, where control-flow flattening and bogus branches would hurt the benchmark's runtime the most; SPLIT stays a low-risk diversity helper. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low across all passes given the clean round-1 result, with IGV slightly higher since global-variable encodings carry the most semantic risk in FP code.
